note: Adapted from the original English description of Krishna & Emerson 1962 (new species; type locality Tchibinda forest, Mt. Bukulumusa above Mulungu, Congo, altitude 2250—2300 m); based only on 10 soldiers, the original does not describe the alate or the worker. Measurements are translated verbatim from Table 12 of the original, in millimetres. The diagnostic characters of the original give the antennae as 12-segmented while its soldier description gives 13; both figures are retained.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Compared with G. kawandae the head is slightly narrower, the mandibles have no distinct basal tubercle, the proximal half of the postmentum is more strongly constricted, and the pronotum is narrower with the posterior margin distinctly emarginate in the middle; compared with G. insulanus the head is larger, the anterior dorsal swelling of the frons weaker, the mandibles shorter and stouter, the sides of the anterior third of the postmentum nearly parallel, the antennae 12-segmented, and the pronotum larger with an angulate anterior margin and a slightly emarginate posterior margin; in G. parki all parts are smaller and the anterior dorsal swelling of the frons is indistinct; in G. longuisculus all parts are smaller and the anterior dorsal swelling of the frons is weaker.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head reddish brown, the frons dark brown almost black; mandibles shining, black, blackish brown at the base; postmentum reddish brown with a dark brown band on each side; pronotum concolorous with the posterior part of the head and with yellow patches; labrum and legs pale yellow; antennae brownish; tergites pale yellowish brown. Head with a few scattered erect setae; pronotal margins and disc with long and short setae; labrum with about 9—10 long setae. Head long and stout; sides almost parallel, slightly concave near the middle; the median depression of the frons broad; anterior dorsal swellings moderately distinct; frontal slope about 60° in lateral view. Y suture visible. Compound eyes small, hidden by the dark colour of the head. Sides of the labrum converging forwards to a blunt point. Mandibles short and stout, the outer margin evenly rounded; left mandible with 3 marginal teeth; right mandible with 2 marginal teeth, the tip of the 1st marginal tooth 0.38 mm from the apical tooth. Proximal half of the postmentum markedly constricted, the greatest width slightly more than 2 times the narrowest; anterior margin straight. Antennae 13-segmented, segment 2 longer than segments 3 and 4, segment 3 shorter than segment 4. Pronotum slightly narrower than the head; anterior margin concave; posterolateral corners broadly rounded; posterior margin nearly straight. Femora moderately swollen. Measurements (mm; 10 soldiers, means in parentheses): head length (to the lateral base of the mandibles) 1.88—2.10 (2.00); head width 1.20—1.26 (1.22); head height 1.13—1.14 (1.13); left mandible length 0.94—0.96 (0.95); postmentum maximum width 0.49—0.53 (0.51), minimum width 0.21—0.23 (0.22), length 1.28—1.54 (1.43); pronotal median length 0.58—0.64 (0.61), maximum length 0.68—0.75 (0.72), width 1.09—1.16 (1.13); hind tibia length 0.82—0.93 (0.90).
